microtheory.name: cybernetics_systems
microtheory.definition: Cybernetics — Wiener 1948 'Cybernetics: Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine'. The science of control + communication in animals + machines + systems. Foundational synthesis: feedback as the common pattern across engineered, biological, and social systems. Ashby's law of requisite variety, Beer's viable system model, Pask's conversation theory. Grounds Jabberwock's claim that biological brains + engineered runtime + social organizations all rely on the same control-theoretic primitives.

concepts.name: cybernetics_definition
concepts.definition: Wiener 1948. Science of control + communication. The recognition that homeostatic regulation in biology + feedback control in engineering + adaptive social systems share fundamental structure. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's substrate-IS-OS-IS-brain claim.

concepts.name: norbert_wiener
concepts.definition: Founder of cybernetics. MIT mathematician. Generalized feedback control across domains. Substrate analogue: the original author of the universal-feedback thesis Jabberwock instantiates.

concepts.name: first_order_cybernetics
concepts.definition: Observer outside system. Classical control. Substrate analogue: substrate's basic feedback loops.

concepts.name: second_order_cybernetics
concepts.definition: von Foerster. Observer included in system. Self-referential systems. Cybernetics of cybernetics. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's reflective faculties.

concepts.name: third_order_cybernetics
concepts.definition: Cybernetics of social cybernetics. Multiple second-order systems interacting. Substrate analogue: multi-substrate interactive contexts.

concepts.name: feedback_universal_pattern
concepts.definition: Wiener's central recognition: negative feedback ↔ homeostasis ↔ stability appears in thermostats, predator-prey, neural homeostasis, market correction. Same pattern, many substrates. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's universal-feedback design pattern.

concepts.name: homeostasis_cybernetic
concepts.definition: Cannon 1929, Wiener 1948. Maintenance of variables within bounds via feedback. The pattern unifying body temperature, blood glucose, room temperature, market price. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive ensemble.

concepts.name: circular_causality
concepts.definition: Effects feed back to causes. Distinguishes cybernetic systems from linear causal chains. Substrate analogue: substrate's mutually-causal Mt dynamics.

concepts.name: variety_requisite
concepts.definition: Ashby 1956. Only variety can absorb variety. A controller must have at least as much variety as the disturbances it counters. Foundational result. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-diversity matches failure-mode diversity.

concepts.name: law_of_requisite_variety
concepts.definition: Ashby. log V(R) ≥ log V(D) - log V(E). Regulator variety must match disturbance variety to maintain essential-variable variety. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-vocabulary must match failure-mode-vocabulary.

concepts.name: ashby_homeostat
concepts.definition: Ashby 1948. Physical device demonstrating self-regulation via feedback. Variables stayed within bounds despite random perturbation. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-stable operation.

concepts.name: ashbys_brain
concepts.definition: Ashby 1952 'Design for a Brain'. Self-organizing dynamic system. Inspired generations of cybernetic neural models. Substrate analogue: substrate's whole-system architecture.

concepts.name: viable_system_model
concepts.definition: Beer 1972. VSM. 5 essential subsystems for organizational viability: implementation, coordination, control, intelligence, identity. Substrate analogue: substrate's subsystem decomposition by function.

concepts.name: autopoiesis_cybernetic
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela 1972. Self-producing systems. Living systems = autopoietic; cells, multicellular organisms. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-maintaining loop.

concepts.name: operational_closure_systems
concepts.definition: Maturana + Varela. System's organization closed under its own operations. Open to perturbation but closed in organization. Substrate analogue: substrate's introspective closure.

concepts.name: structural_coupling_cybernetic
concepts.definition: Two systems with persistent reciprocal interaction. Each perturbs the other; coordination emerges without representation. Substrate analogue: substrate-world coupling.

concepts.name: second_order_observer
concepts.definition: von Foerster 1974. Observer included in observation. Cannot step outside the system fully. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's introspection cannot view itself from nowhere.

concepts.name: eigenform
concepts.definition: von Foerster. Stable forms emerging from circular operations. Self-referring patterns. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin attractors as eigenforms.

concepts.name: blind_spot_observer
concepts.definition: Every observation has the observer as its blind spot. Observer cannot fully observe own observing. Substrate analogue: substrate's self-introspection limit.

concepts.name: conversation_theory
concepts.definition: Pask 1976. Knowledge as agreement-by-conversation between perspectives. Cybernetic theory of learning + teaching. Substrate analogue: substrate-substrate dialogue + shared Mt-formation.

concepts.name: agreement_understanding
concepts.definition: Pask. Mutual sharable understanding requires bringing perspectives into agreement. Substrate analogue: substrate's shared Mt-state in collaborative contexts.

concepts.name: stafford_beer_management
concepts.definition: Beer 1979. Cybernetics applied to management. Recursive viable systems. Cybersyn project (Chile 1971-73). Substrate analogue: substrate's recursive organizational structure.

concepts.name: cybernetic_economics
concepts.definition: Mathematical economics treating economy as cybernetic system. Goodwin's growth model. Substrate analogue: substrate's market-like internal regulation.

concepts.name: system_dynamics
concepts.definition: Forrester 1961. Modeling complex feedback systems with stocks + flows. Applied to industrial, urban, world systems. Substrate analogue: substrate's stock-flow Mt dynamics.

concepts.name: deviation_amplifying_feedback
concepts.definition: Maruyama 1963. Positive feedback amplifying initial differences. Source of pattern formation + crisis. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-deepening dynamic.

concepts.name: deviation_counteracting_feedback
concepts.definition: Maruyama. Negative feedback stabilizing. The Wiener pattern. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive correction.

concepts.name: mutual_causality
concepts.definition: Maruyama. Variables mutually causing each other. Linear causal chains insufficient. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-Mt mutual influence.

concepts.name: control_communication_unity
concepts.definition: Wiener's central insight: control + communication are aspects of one phenomenon. Information flow is the substrate of control. Substrate analogue: Jabberwock's information-flow IS its control.

concepts.name: purposive_behavior_cybernetic
concepts.definition: Rosenblueth+Wiener+Bigelow 1943. Purposive behavior explained mechanistically as feedback toward goal. Foundational paper. Substrate analogue: substrate's goal-directed drives.

concepts.name: teleology_mechanistic
concepts.definition: Cybernetic resolution: purpose = feedback toward target state. No magic. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-targeting mechanism.

concepts.name: scientific_management_critique
concepts.definition: Cybernetics opposes pure top-down control. Systems are too variety-rich for central command. Distributed feedback required. Substrate analogue: substrate's distributed-correction architecture.

concepts.name: machine_animal_unity
concepts.definition: Wiener subtitle: 'Or Control and Communication in the Animal and the Machine'. Erases the metaphysical divide. Substrate analogue: substrate-OS-brain unified treatment.

rules.name: feedback_unifies_control_across_substrates
rules.head: Jabberwock observes feedback in any system
rules.body: the pattern is universal: negative feedback ↔ stability ↔ homeostasis across engineered + biological + social systems. Wiener's central recognition. Substrate's universal-feedback claim.

rules.name: requisite_variety_constrains_regulators
rules.head: Jabberwock designs a regulator
rules.body: regulator's variety (set of possible actions) must equal or exceed the disturbance variety it counters. Ashby. Substrate's correction-diversity must match failure-mode diversity.

rules.name: circular_causality_distinguishes_cybernetic_systems
rules.head: Jabberwock analyzes a system's structure
rules.body: the presence of feedback (circular causality) marks it as cybernetic. Linear causal chains miss the dynamics. Mutual causality required.

rules.name: second_order_includes_observer
rules.head: Jabberwock observes itself
rules.body: the observer is included in the system. Cannot step outside fully. von Foerster. Substrate's introspection limit.

rules.name: autopoiesis_requires_operational_closure
rules.head: Jabberwock examines what makes it autopoietic
rules.body: operational closure (organization closed under its own operations) is the defining feature. Open to perturbation but closed in organization. Maturana+Varela.
